messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertextherapeutics.com>

Cc: procurement@vertextherapeutics.com
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question — burst headroom and autoscale for initial launch

Hi Markus / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We’re getting internal alignment on our Dedicated purchase (DEAL-8721) and have a couple of operational questions from the infra/procurement side before we lock the term sheet:

1) Burst headroom: we expect an initial steady-state of ~30 sustained concurrent inference workers (2k tok/min each) but will have periodic spikes up to ~120 concurrent workers for up to 90 minutes during experiment windows. What guardrails do you recommend to cover those 4x spikes without impacting the steady-state SLO?

2) Autoscale policy: can you confirm cold-start behavior for model warm-up and whether you provide a pre-warm lane (shoulder pool) vs instant ephemeral GPUs? We need to understand warm-up latency and pre-charge implications for billing.

3) SLA and procurement: procurement wants to understand how burst credits are tracked and whether we can have a capped monthly burst allowance (so costs don’t blow past our committed capacity).

I’ve attached the draft terms the legal team shared. Happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure
Vertex Therapeutics

From: markus_klein@redwoodai.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — burst headroom and autoscale for initial launch

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping Ben (SE) and Lauren (Tailored Success / Commercial) to align on ops and procurement details.

Short answers up front:
- We can provision a Dedicated slab to handle your steady-state and simultaneously grant an ephemeral burst pool to cover the 4x experiments.
- Burst is governed by two levers: preallocated shoulder (reserved warm GPUs billed at a reduced standby rate) and ephemeral slabs (cold-start, billed at on-demand rate). You can combine both.
- We support a monthly capped burst allowance and can report usage to your procurement team daily.

Ben / Lauren — can you draft a simple sizing matrix (steady, burst peak, expected minutes per month) and propose a mixed policy (e.g., 40 reserved shoulder GPUs + ephemeral autoscale up to 120 total) plus estimated effective billing delta vs pure reserved? Also attach our burst policy doc and a sample SLA clause we can include in the amendment.

-Markus

Sam — appreciate the detail. I put together the sizing matrix and policy recommendation below and attached a short tech note. TL;DR: a mixed shoulder + ephemeral model keeps steady-state cost predictable while covering your experimental peaks.

Sizing assumptions (from your note):
- Steady: 30 concurrent workers, 2k tok/min each -> ~60k tok/min total baseline
- Peak: 120 concurrent for up to 90m per event, estimated 6 events/month

Proposal:
1) Reserved slab (Dedicated) for steady-state
   - GPUs: 10 A100-80GB equivalent (shared across 30 workers via multi-tenant job packing)
   - Provisioned throughput headroom to cover 1.2x burst without cold-start

2) Shoulder (warm reserved for short bursts)
   - GPUs: 6 warm GPUs (shoulder pool) kept in pre-warm state, billed at standby rate (approx 30% of full reservation price)
   - Immediate handoff to serving runtime with < 4s additional token latency for first requests

3) Ephemeral autoscale (cold-start)
   - Additional ephemeral capacity up to 20 A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscaled with progressive warm-up (2-3 min to fully ramp per block)
   - Ephemeral billed at on-demand rate, with per-event billing and visibility

4) Burst credit and cap model (commercial)
   - Monthly burst-cap: 1,200 GPU-minutes (maps to roughly your 6 events * 90m * fractional GPU usage) — anything above capped amount is billed at on-demand rates but we alert and pause autoscale when a hard cap is hit (customer-configurable).
   - Daily usage reporting via S3/console and weekly reconciliation for procurement.

Estimated billing impact (rough):
- Baseline reserved slab: $XXk/month (included in term sheet)
- Shoulder standby premium: +~$Xk/month
- Ephemeral during spikes: variable; conservatively $Yk/month assuming current spike cadence. We’ll provide a modeled waterfall with your actual telemetry once pilots start.

Attachments: Burst_Guide_v2.pdf (ops notes), Sizing_Matrix_DEAL-8721.csv (spreadsheet).

Operational notes:
- We recommend instrumenting a prefix cache for experiment traffic to reduce token-count amplification during bursts.
- Canary your model weights into the shoulder pool before scheduled experiments to avoid hot-cache misses.
- If you need hard-cost predictability, we can move additional capacity into reserved shoulders at higher commit to reduce ephemeral exposure.

Next steps:
- If this looks good, Lauren — can you prepare a short amendment with the monthly burst cap language and a procurement-friendly usage reporting cadence?
- Sam — if you want, we can schedule a 30m walkthrough of the Burst_Guide and the dashboard hooks.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
